messages.author: 2e9423a4b20e1401
messages.subject: Feature request - graph structure
parts:
I'd like to request a feature. Hierarchical models tend to have a sparse Hessian, and the trustOptim R package gives fast optimization, based on a specification of the sparsity structure of the Hessian. This can be determined from the dependency graph of the model. Having this graph structure available for a given Stan model could, for example, lead to much faster Laplace approximations.

I'm not familiar with Stan's C++ code. But the graph we want is essentially that there is an edge between two variables if those variables occur together in a term of the log posterior. Is this readily available, or do you have any feel for how difficult this would be to extract and export to R? Any plans for this or anything similar already in the works?

Thanks,
Chad

On 8/28/13 11:35 AM, Chad Scherrer wrote:
> I'd like to request a feature. Hierarchical models tend to have a sparse Hessian, and the trustOptim
> <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/trustOptim/vignettes/trustOptim-vignette.pdf> R package gives fast optimization,

> based on a specification of the sparsity structure of the Hessian. This can be determined from the dependency graph of
> the model. Having this graph structure available for a given Stan model could, for example, lead to much faster Laplace
> approximations.
>
> I'm not familiar with Stan's C++ code. But the graph we want is essentially that there is an edge between two variables
> if those variables occur together in a term of the log posterior. Is this readily available, or do you have any feel for
> how difficult this would be to extract and export to R? Any plans for this or anything similar already in the works?

The problem is that there's no notion of graphical model behind
Stan. It's just a log probability function that's proportional
to the posterior p(theta|y) where theta are params and y is data.
This can be structured like a directed graphical
model for the joint p(y,theta), but there's nothing in the language
that lets us extract the (implicit) graph.

We also don't have any sparse matrix algebra plugged in, though
Eigen's added a bunch more support and brought it into the mainstream
of their package. I know almost nothing about the math behind this,
so I'm not the right person to ask about our doing this any time soon.
It's definitely relevant to other things we're doing, too, like
Riemann Manifold HMC, which might have a structured sparse Hessian which could
greatly speed up some of the algebraic operations.

- Bolb

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Feature request - graph structure
parts:
Bob,

You're right that we can't get the graphical model out from a Stan model, but I think Chad may be referring to something that we could (in theory) do.  Basically, imagine doing an analysis of the model and every time a set of parameters appeared in the same expression, those parameters had an edge stuck between them.  The resulting graph would tell you something about the sparsity structure of the Hessian.  Basically, it's static code analysis for Stan.

Anyway, it's possible but not really on our radar right now.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Feature request - graph structure
parts: On Wed, Aug 28, 2013 at 3:55 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

Nifty.  If x1 and x2 never showed up together
in a subexpression, then dx1.dx2 f(x) = 0.
Exactly.

It's still tricky when we have iterative or branching algorithms,
because what shows up together can vary by iteration.

The easiest way to do this is to be very conservative and effectively assume every branch is both true and false.  This is effectively equivalent to computing graphs for every possible set of branching possibilities and then taking the edge-wise or of them but can be done without the combinatorial explosion.

There's also some tricky bits in tracking intermediary variables and expressions but it's all doable.

Cheers,
Marcus

- Bob

> edge-wise or of them but can be done without the combinatorial explosion.
>
> There's also some tricky bits in tracking intermediary variables and expressions but it's all doable.

Don't we run into undecidability issues? We also have intermediate
values that can be calculated to determine loop indices and we
also have iterations (like for and while loops) that lead to
problems.

One thing I've thought about is supporting a more restrictive modeling
language for which we can compute these things. These are all issues
for doing discrete sampling, where we want to somehow compute the Markov
blanket of a discrete variable.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Feature request - graph structure
parts:
Yeah, this is basically computing something like a Markov blanket in the continuous case.  For something like this (computing the Hessian sparsity pattern) or with the Markov blanket I think the only way we could do it is as you suggest, by restricting what people can do with the modelling language.

Alternatively, it could be done on the fly as a post-hoc analysis of the expression tree generated from the autodiff but it would have to be done for each iteration.

Cheers,
Marcus

Hessian structure is a slightly more holistic problem than calculating
a Markov blanket for a discrete parameter.

What Marcus is suggesting will work --- checking the
dependencies on each log prob calc. But it'd be relatively
slow compared to calculating everything up front in a more
limited language or figuring out some way to specify the
structure.

- Bob
